name: Khan ez-Zeit mouth, west side (y 479-487)
why: D41 (KeZ north looking S from the fork, shops closed): openings ~2.2-3 m x 2.8-3.2 m under flat steel lintels, multi-leaf panelled steel doors (4-6 leaves) painted grey, beige and olive (atlas door_olive, the multi-leaf cell) and grey roll-downs, no teal or green; raised stone thresholds 0.15-0.2 m; corrugated canopies from both sides over the open bays; white hanging boards. At the D41 camera (beside it, out of frame on the right); the mouth is 5.5-9.4 m wall to wall (notes 1.6) and this front faces the fork. Doors as the rest of the row in D41.
